result.summary: This PR (open since 2017, based on #29409) adds an --enable-multiprocess build option producing bitcoin-node, bitcoin-wallet, and bitcoin-gui executables that communicate over Cap'n Proto IPC instead of running in one process. It wraps the Node, Wallet, and Chain interfaces in capnp serialization code, adds process-spawning logic (bitcoin-gui spawns bitcoin-node, which spawns bitcoin-wallet), and bundles the libmultiprocess subtree plus its CI configuration. The current diff also includes real bug fixes uncovered along the way: eager destruction of disconnected btcsignals callbacks (fixing a hang in interface_gui.py) and an atomic<shared_ptr> fallback for platforms lacking C++20 support.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core historically runs node, wallet, and GUI code in one process, which couples their crash domains, complicates running components with different trust or resource requirements, and (per gmaxwell, laanwj, sipa in the discussion) has long been seen as an architectural improvement worth making. This PR is the foundational step for reviewers, maintainers, and future consumers of the process-separation project (issue #28722) who want the wallet and GUI to run independently of the node.

open_concerns: Whether Cap'n Proto is the right long-term IPC protocol was raised early (jonasschnelli, dcousens, gmaxwell) but scoped out of this PR by design (ryanofsky, laanwj); no active objection remains.
sipa's early question about the actual benefit of process separation was answered (it's a first step toward optional independent operation) and not revisited.

External testers (Sjors, jimhashhq) reported various rough edges (log file naming, -ipcconnect gaps, GUI not honoring config sections) which the author has been iteratively fixing across years of rebases.
resolved_concerns: laanwj's and reviewers' architectural questions about parameter passing, async calls, and UI integration were answered and incorporated into later revisions.
A dead-pointer bug found by practicalswift was fixed.
discussion.author_status: active, most recently rebasing on 2026 dates to resolve conflicts with concurrently merged PRs; author_silent_days is only 9

reviewability.label: Ready
reviewability.reason: No known open material request is blocking review: needs_rebase is false, CI is not failing, and author_silent_days (9) is far under the staleness threshold. The main caution is that this PR has been force-pushed 107 times over nine years to keep pace with the rest of the codebase, so a review done today may be invalidated by the next rebase; reviewers should expect to review the stable capnp-wrapper commits rather than every rebase diff.

agreement.summary: Broad, long-standing concept support from many maintainers (laanwj, gmaxwell, jonasschnelli, dcousens, jamesob, hebasto, promag) with one old, unfollowed concept NACK (electorr) and an early protocol-choice preference (dcousens wanted RPC over capnp) that was resolved by agreeing the protocol is swappable and out of scope.
agreement.reason: Multiple reviewers stated specific, substantive reasons to want this (better GUI responsiveness, cleaner separation, unblocking future independent operation), and no reviewer treats the current design as blocking. The standing caveat is that some reviewers would have preferred a different serialization protocol, which the author explicitly declined to change, framing it as an implementation detail hidden behind two files.

Whether maintainers currently intend to merge this before or after sibling PRs (#31740, #31741, #19460, #19461) is unclear from the discussion; order seems flexible per ryanofsky's own comments.
The exact current state of the concept NACK from electorr (very early in the thread, likely stale) is not clear; I treated it as unresolved but inactive rather than a live blocker.

Some category memberships (rpc, tools) are thin — mostly one or two lines — and could arguably be excluded as merely mechanical follow-on; I included them per the inclusive-membership rule but flagged low scores.
result.card: This nine-year-old draft PR is the foundational piece of Bitcoin Core's process-separation project: it adds an --enable-multiprocess build producing separate bitcoin-node, bitcoin-wallet, and bitcoin-gui executables that talk over a Cap'n Proto IPC layer instead of sharing one process. It directly unblocks two dependent open PRs (#19460, #19461) and the process-separation project tracked in issue #28722, and along the way fixes a real bug where disconnected signal callbacks stayed alive and hung interface_gui.py, plus portability fixes for macOS/FreeBSD/sanitizer builds. Review sentiment has been strongly positive for years from laanwj, gmaxwell, jonasschnelli, dcousens, jamesob, hebasto, and promag, with one old, unfollowed concept NACK and an early protocol-choice preference that the author deliberately left unresolved by scoping capnp usage to two isolated files. The PR is reviewable now with no known blocking request open, though it has been force-pushed 107 times and continues to be rebased against the fast-moving codebase, so reviews can be invalidated by the next rebase. It is huge (about 4000 lines added across 136 files) and spans ipc, build, wallet, rpc, tests, tools, docs, and utils, but its importance is overwhelmingly concentrated in the ipc category as the project's central unblocking change.
